desc:
The array nums of non-negative integers may contain repeated values. Two subsets are considered the same when they contain every value the same number of times, no matter which positions the values come from. The empty subset has sum 0 and is a subset like any other.

Return the number of distinct subsets whose sum is between lo and hi inclusive, modulo 1,000,000,007.
constraints: The sum of all elements is at most 3,000
hints: Count the multiplicity of every distinct value. A distinct subset is a choice of how many copies of each value to take.
That is a bounded knapsack over sums 0..hi: dp[s] = number of ways to reach sum s with the values handled so far. The value 0 is special, it never changes a sum.
For a value v with c copies, the new table is new[s] = dp[s] + dp[s-v] + ... + dp[s-c*v]. Compute it in O(1) per cell with new[s] = new[s-v] + dp[s] - dp[s-(c+1)*v].
editorial: Zeros are free: if the value 0 occurs z times, every other selection can be extended with 0 to z zeros, which multiplies the answer by z + 1. Start the table with dp[0] = z + 1 and treat the other values.

For each distinct positive value v occurring c times the new table is new[s] = sum of dp[s - j*v] for j = 0..c. A sliding-window identity makes this O(1) per cell: new[s-v] = sum of dp[s - j*v] for j = 1..c+1, so new[s] = new[s-v] + dp[s] - dp[s-(c+1)*v] (the last term is zero when the index is negative). Every operation is taken modulo 109+7.
Because the total sum is at most 3,000, there are only about 77 distinct positive values (1 + 2 + ... + 77 > 3,000), so the work is about 77 · 3,000 cell updates. The answer is the sum of dp[lo..hi].
time: O(d · hi + n) where d = distinct values
